purpose: This medicine is used to treat mild to moderate COVID-19 in adults and children (12 years and older, weighing at least 40 kg) who are at high risk of getting very sick. It helps keep the infection from getting worse and reduces the chance of being hospitalized. It works best when started as soon as possible after testing positive, ideally within 5 days of symptoms starting.
how_it_works: The COVID-19 virus needs special proteins to copy itself and spread in your body. Nirmatrelvir blocks one of those proteins so the virus cannot make more copies of itself. Ritonavir is added not to fight the virus directly, but to slow down how quickly your body breaks down nirmatrelvir, helping it stay in your system long enough to do its job.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are an altered or metallic taste in your mouth, diarrhea, high blood pressure, and muscle aches. Some people also feel nauseous or have headaches. These are usually mild and go away after you finish the course of treatment.
warnings: This medication interacts with MANY common drugs — including some heart medications, cholesterol drugs, blood thinners, and others — so it is very important to tell your doctor and pharmacist about everything you take. It should not be used in certain people with severe kidney or liver problems. Do not take it if you are pregnant without talking to your doctor first. If your COVID symptoms come back after finishing the course (called rebound), contact your healthcare provider.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 2 pink nirmatrelvir tablets plus 1 white ritonavir tablet taken together by mouth, twice a day (morning and evening), for 5 days. Take them with or without food. Try to take them at the same times each day, and finish the full 5-day course even if you start feeling better.
